title: Architecture
content:
Build and delivery

authorized material
  → evidence admission
  → SemanticProposal
  → validation and review
  → KnowledgeRevision
  ├→ 3D ontology graph → human review
  └→ CognitivePackageDraft → A3S Use generation → A3S Code / Agent

Domain model {#domain-model}

Workspace: authority boundary for organizational knowledge, grants, and ontology revisions.

KnowledgeScope: the material, version, and processing boundary admitted to one build.

Evidence: admitted, citable material.

SemanticProposal: a candidate concept, relationship, or claim proposed by an Agent.

KnowledgeRevision: an immutable, approval-bound knowledge revision with one exact parent.

CognitivePackageDraft: a schema-v3 package draft containing surfaces such as OKF and Skill; direct revision-only input is still being migrated.

Package generation: the exact package installed, locked, and published by A3S Use for Agents.

The 3D graph is a human-review projection of KnowledgeRevision, not an Agent query interface.

The Rust engine binds each LearningProject, ResourceSet, and admitted source
to one Organization, Workspace authority generation, and immutable
KnowledgeScope revision. Scope selectors, allowed formats, and budgets are
checked before acquisition. Each exact scope revision also has a durable,
digest-addressed source inventory: monotonic observations reconcile into
immutable versions or removal tombstones, and conflicts leave the prior
snapshot unchanged. Every build now freezes that complete snapshot plus the
exact versions of its explicitly declared sources into project intent,
admission, and package provenance. Removed, changed, or resolver-drifted
sources fail before parsing. Each
logical scope has a durable compare-and-swap active scope revision; configured
source reads hold a shared lease and reject missing, stale, or revoked revisions
before opening source content.

After exact human approval, the engine compiles or reuses an immutable
KnowledgeRevision. It binds the frozen scope/inventory, source and document
sets, grounded claims/concepts/procedures/conflicts, excerpt-free evidence
producer identities, approval/report/policy digests, compiler generation, and
exact parent. Package-only Skill guidance is excluded from ontology authority.
A separate Workspace-wide head advances through exact-parent compare-and-swap;
the object is persisted first, exact replay does not advance generation, and
corrupt or competing state fails closed.

The CLI records source-version → document → evidence → revision →
revision-bound draft dependencies before activation, so source or whole-scope
queries include the approved revision in their digest-bound impact closure.
Graph and A3S Use generation invalidation remain separate authority operations.
The package compiler still consumes the approved package directly and does not
yet embed the revision digest, so end-to-end revision-to-package lineage is not
claimed in v0.1.

Parser-backed evidence is also bound to the exact generated capability matrix
from the reviewed Parser generation. Only qualified DOCX, XLSX, PPTX, PDF, and
image rows may enter semantic projection; detected-format, media-type, natural
unit, or unsupported legacy-format drift fails closed. The provenance keeps
the matrix digest and honest structural, visual, caller-provided, or
feature-gated status without exposing Parser repository paths.

Release assurance remains separate. A pinned policy plus an independently
reviewed exact receipt must cover all five profiles and passed provider, resume,
Linux, macOS, and Windows evidence. Missing, failed, or unavailable results fail
closed. Version 0.1 does not bundle a passing receipt and therefore does not
claim cross-platform Parser release qualification.

Model input uses prompt-contract v2. Fixed system/task/schema/envelope
instructions share one recorded digest, while context and evidence are
length- and SHA-256-bound JSON with framing delimiters escaped. Locale tags
cannot add prompt lines, and closed proposals cannot add Tool, permission,
package, or approval authority.

Decoded semantic values are reconstructed before evaluation. Stable IDs and
map keys must agree, relationships require admitted evidence, and self or
dangling edges, duplicate conflicts, and non-canonical bounded fields fail
closed.

A3S component boundaries

Component	Role	Does not own
A3S Use	Validate the package, resolve dependencies, then install, lock, and publish a generation	Generate or approve the ontology
A3S Code	Run ontology Agents and host business Agents against an exact generation	Read the 3D graph directly
A3S Flow	Keep durable exploration, ingestion, compilation, and evaluation history	Knowledge authority
A3S Cloud	Deploy roles, nodes, routes, Secrets, and Runtime Tasks	KnowledgeScope or ontology revisions

Quality {#quality}

Quality covers citation completeness, authorization correctness, reproducible revisions and package generations, language/version parity, and prevention of implementation disclosure in public artifacts.

title: Agentic Ontology documentation
content:
Agentic Ontology compiles authorized documents into ontology revisions and produces two artifacts from each revision: a 3D graph for human review and a schema-v3 cognitive package for A3S Use. Agents do not access the graph. They consume an exact package generation installed, locked, and published by A3S Use.

Current public surface

The product site explains the path from documents and evidence to an ontology revision and cognitive package.

The 3D Playground uses mock semantic data to demonstrate the complete interaction model.

A public artifact generator produces the Playground contract and can later accept real semantic build output.

Public artifacts contain no source code, code snippets, repository paths, line numbers, Git history, or source maps.

Start here

Quick start

Playground

Architecture

Public data boundary

Versioning

Playground counts, timestamps, relationships, and package content are demo data. They are not production scale, performance, or delivery claims. No package is installed, locked, or published yet.

title: Playground
content:
The Playground demonstrates the complete Agentic Ontology product shape; it is not a source-code browser. It currently uses build-generated mock data, with all demo values labelled honestly.

Three linked regions

Agent learning events

The left ledger records when an Agent read a public document, which knowledge it understood, which semantics it created, and which Ontology Revision received the change. Selecting an event highlights related graph nodes and edges.

Semantic 3D ontology

The center graph uses a restrained structural grayscale and supports search, filtering, camera focus, neighborhood highlighting, and recentering. People can switch to the keyboard semantic list at any time; environments without WebGL enter the same list automatically and retain node and relationship navigation.

The center surface can also switch to the build run. That view replays the same mock run across six stages: scope admission, evidence build, proposal review, revision compile, package publication, and Agent evaluation. Every stage shows its product object, execution authority, deterministic gate, and receipt. The current demo honestly stops before A3S Use publication, so Agent evaluation is blocked.

Cognitive-package preview

The right panel shows the schema-v3 cognitive package planned from the current KnowledgeRevision, including its identity, OKF and Skill surfaces, and the path from draft through A3S Use installation, locking, and publication to an A3S Code Agent. The current state is explicitly preview, not-installed, not-locked, and not-published.

Delivery boundary {#delivery-boundary}

The graph is only for human search, focus, review, and traceability.

Agents do not access the graph, and no public graph-query payload exists.

The mock package draft models the target KnowledgeRevision binding and lists its OKF and Skill surfaces; current Rust package bytes do not yet embed that revision digest.

A3S Code only consumes an exact generation installed, locked, and published by A3S Use.

Complete, waiting, and blocked states in the build run are mock-run states, not claims that production capabilities have shipped.

title: Quick start
content:
Requirements

Node.js 22 or newer

npm 11

Local development

npm install
npm run dev

The product site uses /agentic-ontology/ as its default repository base path. To work on the 3D Playground directly:

npm run dev:playground

Build every static artifact

npm run build

The build generates the public semantic artifact, builds the Playground, product site, and versioned docs, assembles them under website/doc_build/, and then runs route and privacy checks.

First verification

Open the product home and confirm Simplified Chinese is the default.

Open the Playground and select a learning event.

Confirm the 3D graph highlights related nodes and relationships.

Inspect the cognitive-package preview and confirm that it is marked draft, not installed, not locked, and not published.

title: Versioning
content:
Documentation versions both product state and language. The default version and default language use paths without prefixes.

Content	Path
v0.1 Simplified Chinese	/agentic-ontology/docs/
v0.1 English	/agentic-ontology/docs/en/
next Simplified Chinese	/agentic-ontology/docs/next/
next English	/agentic-ontology/docs/next/en/

v0.1 records the current demo contract. next describes unreleased evolution. Every version must contain the same page set in Chinese and English; the build fails on translation-page drift.
